title.value: Can Ensembling Pre-processing Algorithms Lead to Better Machine Learning Fairness?
title.justification: This value is based on the explicit mention in the paper's title as provided by the authors.
title.quote: Can Ensembling Pre-processing Algorithms Lead to Better Machine Learning Fairness?

extractions.description: This paper evaluates the potential for combining multiple fairness pre-processing algorithms into an ensemble to improve machine learning fairness. It analyzes three popular fairness pre-processing algorithms and investigates the robustness of an ensemble approach in mitigating bias while maintaining accuracy in machine learning models.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The paper's central theme is about enhancing fairness in machine learning systems, primarily focusing on socio-economic impacts, but it does not directly address Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development as its main topic.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: As machine learning (ML) systems get adopted in more critical areas, it has become increasingly crucial to address the bias that could occur in these systems.

primary_category.justification: The paper addresses fairness in machine learning without a direct connection to Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development. It does not discuss topics like climate change mitigation, natural systems protection, pollution, etc.
primary_category.quote: Numerous examples of biased ML systems exist, each causing severe socio-economical consequences to their users.

secondary_categories.justification: The focus remains outside the scope of Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development themes even when considering secondary categories.
secondary_categories.quote: The objective of these algorithms is to promote fairness in a statistical sense, meaning that the algorithms try to transform the dataset to have an equal distributive representation of a specified protected attribute to prompt a fairer model.

primary_sub_category.justification: No specific sub-category directly related to Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development is addressed in the paper.
primary_sub_category.quote: This work evaluates three popular fairness pre-processing algorithms and investigates the potential for combining all algorithms into a more robust pre-processing ensemble.

secondary_sub_categories.justification: Since the paper does not cover any area of Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development, it doesn't fit any secondary sub-categories either.
secondary_sub_categories.quote: Fairness pre-processing algorithms provide different trade-offs, which raises challenges for practitioners to select the best algorithm for their ML systems.

applications.justification: The applications of the paper are related to machine learning fairness, not directly applicable to climate or ecological issues.
applications.quote: Specifically, we investigate whether ensembling multiple fairness pre-processing algorithms can provide further improvements to the model’s fairness and accuracy.

new_primary_category.justification: The existing categories and sub-categories of Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development do not apply to the paper. Hence, no new category is needed.
new_primary_category.quote: We evaluate the performance of several fairness pre-processing algorithms to highlight their strengths and weaknesses in fairness and accuracy.

new_primary_sub_category.justification: The paper does not address Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development, so no new sub-category related to these themes is necessary.
new_primary_sub_category.quote: We provide practitioners with empirical evidence on the performance of three popular fairness pre-processing algorithms by highlighting their impact on the model’s fairness and accuracy.
